title: Martín E. De Simone | Education Specialist
gist: A World Bank staff-profile page for education specialist Martín E. De Simone whose post history documents a multi-year (2020-2026) World Bank program deploying generative-AI chatbots in Nigerian classrooms through the Edo Basic Education Sector and Skills Transformation (EdoBESST) initiative, culminating in an August 2026 piece on 'cost-effective AI adoption' in education.

themes.theme: A Multi-Year AI-in-Education Bet in Nigeria

insights.claim: De Simone's most recent listed post, dated August 4, 2026, is titled 'Supporting cost-effective AI adoption in education,' following earlier 2023-2025 posts on generative-AI pilots in Edo State, Nigeria — indicating the World Bank's messaging has shifted from pilot lessons-learned toward cost-effectiveness and scaling of AI in African classrooms.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A multi-year pilot maturing into a 'cost-effective adoption' framing suggests the World Bank sees this as a template for procurement/scaling decisions across other African education systems — worth tracking as a case study for edtech vendors and donor co-financing.
insights.locator: Supporting cost-effective AI adoption in education, August 04, 2026

insights.claim: De Simone was task team leader for the Edo Basic Education Sector and Skills Transformation (EdoBESST) program in Nigeria, which the World Bank has documented through a recurring 'chalkboards to chatbots' post series (2024-2025) on deploying generative-AI tools directly in schools.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: EdoBESST is a concrete, named program to watch for World Bank generative-AI education spending and results data in Sub-Saharan Africa.
insights.locator: task team leader for the Edo Basic Education Sector and Skills Transformation (EdoBESST) program

insights.claim: De Simone helped develop the World Bank's Africa Human Capital Plan and co-led the formulation of the Western and Central Africa Education Strategy, positioning him within the institutional frameworks that set regional education-investment priorities.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
entities: Western and Central Africa Education Strategy
insights.so_what: Names the specific regional strategy documents shaping World Bank education lending pipelines in Africa.
insights.locator: Martín played a key role in developing the Africa Human Capital Plan and co-led the formulation of the Western and Central Africa Education Strategy.
